en.name: Anicetus
en.summary: The pope who received Polycarp of Smyrna in Rome for a landmark, if inconclusive, discussion on the proper date of Easter.
en.body: Anicetus's reign produced one of the best-documented events of the entire early papacy: a visit from Polycarp, the elderly bishop of Smyrna and a disciple of the apostle John, to discuss the Quartodeciman controversy — the disagreement over whether Easter should be tied to the Jewish Passover date or always fall on a Sunday. The two bishops could not agree, but parted amicably, with Anicetus permitting Polycarp to celebrate the Eucharist in Rome as a mark of respect, a detail preserved by the historian Eusebius.
